claims.text: DonHangApp is a StatelessWidget whose build returns a MaterialApp with home: ProductListScreen(apiClient: apiClient); its comment describes it as composing the app shell from small widgets.

ProductListScreen, LoginScreen and CreateOrderScreen are separate widgets in separate files; each constructor requires only an ApiClient; ProductListScreen opens LoginScreen and LoginScreen opens CreateOrderScreen.
In ProductListScreen, each product row is an inline ListTile(title: Text(product.name), trailing: Text(price)) inside ListView.builder's itemBuilder, using only product.
There is no ProductTile class in DonHang.App at stage-1.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: git grep ProductTile (no match in DonHang.App/lib)

claims.text: A StatelessWidget with a final Product field (required in its constructor) whose build returns the same ListTile can replace the inline ListTile.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: StatelessWidget; refs/flutter-website ui (building widgets)

claims.text: A widget also depends on its BuildContext, and ListTile requires a Material ancestor (e.g. Scaffold); what is specific to one use arrives through the constructor.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: ListTile (requires a Material ancestor); StatelessWidget (configuration + BuildContext)

claims.text: SRP applied to widgets: one widget, one reason to change; a widget's constructor parameters are its contract.
setState in a stateful widget rebuilds only that widget's subtree.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: State.setState; refs/flutter-website perf/best-practices.md

claims.text: ListView.builder calls itemBuilder once for each index below itemCount, as rows are needed.
